the following questions: 1.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HEGRA collaboration does not see any evidence for VHE γ-ray emission from any of the 36 sources.
there is no evidence for γ-ray emission above 24 Tev from any of the 36 potential point sources.
there is no indication of any point source of VHE γ-ray emission in the sky.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
no significant VHE γ-rays from point sources have been detected and that the flux limits obtained for the sources observed with AIROBICC are the most stringent ones at energies above 10 TeV.
there is no evidence of point sources in the TeV energy range.
there is no evidence for point sources of γ-rays above 24 Tev.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HEGRA AIROBICC experiment has not detected any of the 36 sources.
the γ-ray sky is not dominated by point sources.
the VHE γ-rays from Mrk 421 are not as intense as expected from the extrapolation of the lower energy data.
